tasks.spec:
You are fixing TWO defects in the LinkedIn half of ONE Python file. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast — edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit. Do NOT git push. Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps; this task needs neither.

YOU OWN EXACTLY TWO FILES:
  1. scripts/identity_proposals.py   (edit it)
  2. fix-summary.md                  (create it)

Touching any other file fails the check.

## What was measured live, this morning

The generator was run against the real candidate inbox with real credentials. HubSpot worked: 5 email proposals for 5 warm referrals. Unipile returned an HTTPError, so all 7 cold candidates came back as 'channel could not be read' and the LinkedIn lane produced nothing.

Two defects, and the second is the dangerous one because it fails silently.

### Defect 1: the request is wrong

`_UnipileProfileClient.search_profiles` issues a GET to /linkedin/search with everything in the query string. The endpoint is a POST, and the search parameters go in a JSON BODY. Known-good shape, taken from tooling that works against this same account today:

    POST https://<dsn>/api/v1/linkedin/search?account_id=<account_id>
    headers: X-API-KEY: <token>, Content-Type: application/json, Accept: application/json
    body:   {"api": "classic", "category": "people", "keywords": <name>, "limit": <limit>}

Note that account_id stays in the QUERY STRING while the search parameters go in the body. Keep returning the parsed JSON object.

### Defect 2: the results would not have matched anybody anyway

Unipile people-search items do not carry a single `name`. They carry `first_name` and `last_name` (and sometimes `display_name`, and `headline`, `location`, `provider_id`). The matching code compares a normalised `name` field, so even a request that succeeded would have found zero plausible matches for everyone — a lane that quietly produces nothing while reporting the channel as read.

So, normalise each returned item before matching: derive `name` from `display_name` when present, otherwise from `first_name` and `last_name` joined; keep `provider_id`, `headline` and `location`. Do this INSIDE the client, so the rest of the file keeps receiving records shaped the way it already expects.

An item with no provider_id, or with no derivable name, is not a candidate match — skip it rather than inventing an identifier.

## What must NOT change

Everything else is verified and stays exactly as it is:

  * exactly one plausible match proposes; two or more propose nobody and record the ambiguity; zero records "no match";
  * a candidate who already has a usable email is never looked up anywhere;
  * a COLD candidate's name is never sent to HubSpot, and a warm one's is never sent to Unipile — every name sent to a source is a disclosure;
  * every proposal carries evidence and a confidence derived from what corroborated it;
  * nothing is applied and nothing is marked confirmed;
  * a source that raises is recorded reached=False with a one-line reason carrying no credential, URL or account identifier, and does not stop the other source;
  * names are carried, intake note text is not;
  * the artifact is written atomically at 0600.

## Run the exact check until it prints PASS

    PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 /mnt/d_drive/repos/loop-factory/ringer/loop-drive-contract/checks/u20_identity_proposals_check.py --worktree "$PWD"

Its LinkedIn fixture now returns the RAW Unipile shape — first_name and last_name as separate fields — so it fails today with cold_not_proposed. That fixture is the reality this code has to survive.

## fix-summary.md

Three sections, using these words as headings: 'What changed', 'How I verified', 'Risk'. Under 'How I verified' paste the actual final output of the check command. Under 'Risk' say what happens if Unipile changes its people-search response shape again. Under 400 words.
tasks.verified: Drives the generator with a LinkedIn fixture returning the raw Unipile people-search shape, so the code must normalise first_name/last_name itself rather than rely on a field Unipile does not send. All the existing assertions still execute — single-match proposes, ambiguous proposes nobody, reachable records are never looked up, cold names never reach HubSpot, no note text, no auto-apply, one dead source degrades only itself, and the real command line with no credentials writes a private explained empty queue.
